steps.title: Paste the product URL
steps.body: Copy the link to any live product page and paste it into the URL to Video field on Home.

steps.title: Review the imported photos
steps.body: AI reads the page and pulls the product photos and description. Keep the shots you want; the badge shows how many were found.

steps.title: Brief the video
steps.body: One or two sentences are enough. Estimated cost is always shown before you commit.

steps.title: Confirm and generate
steps.body: The confirmation modal restates the cost and your balance. Confirming holds the credits; a failed job returns them automatically.

steps.title: Collect from the Library
steps.body: The job moves through generating → finishing → completed. Download within 15 days — everything you keep is yours.

tip.title: Good to know
tip.body: Guests can build the draft without an account; it is restored the moment you sign in.

faq.q: Does the product page need anything special?
faq.a: No. Any public product URL works — AI reads the photos and description that are already on the page.

faq.q: What if the import picks a photo I don't want?
faq.a: Deselect it before briefing. The video is built only from the photos you keep.

faq.q: How much does one video cost?
faq.a: The composer shows the estimated credits before anything runs. Nothing is charged until you confirm.

howto.h1: Bring one product photo to life.
howto.lead: Upload a single product photo and add a short prompt — watch the photo come alive as a moving product clip, ready for ads and social posts.

demo.title: From still to motion →
demo.lead: One photo in, one moving clip out. You describe the action; the model handles camera and motion.

image.alt: Peachy tinted balm product photo on a marble vanity

demo.prompt: She picks it up and takes one swipe — naturally flushed lips

steps.title: Pick one strong photo
steps.body: Clear product, plain background, good light — the same rules as the product-photo field guide.

steps.title: Describe one action
steps.body: Short and concrete beats long and vague. One motion per clip.

steps.title: Check the quote, confirm
steps.body: Cost is shown before you commit; held credits return if the job fails.

steps.title: Compare and keep
steps.body: Generate a variation if the motion feels off; download what you want to keep.

tip.title: Good to know
tip.body: One motion per clip. If you want two actions, generate two clips and keep the better take of each.

faq.q: What kind of photo works best?
faq.a: One clear product, a plain background and even lighting. A phone photo is enough — motion comes from the prompt, not the source image.

faq.q: How long can the clip be?
faq.a: Pick 15 or 30 seconds when you brief the job. The composer shows the cost for each length before you confirm.

faq.q: Can I use the clip in ads?
faq.a: Yes. Download the finished clip from the Library and use it on your product page, in social posts and in ads.

demo.prompt: Morning routine with the tote — coffee, keys, out the door. Natural light.

steps.title: Attach 2–3 references
steps.body: Different angles of the same product beat three near-identical shots.

steps.title: Describe one scene
steps.body: Where, who, what happens. The model fills camera work and pacing.

steps.title: Confirm the quote
steps.body: Cost is shown live; nothing runs until you confirm.

steps.title: Compare versions
steps.body: Generate a variation and keep the stronger take from the Library.

tip.title: Good to know
tip.body: References are just product photos you already have. Every version you generate is kept in the Library, so nothing you try is ever lost.

faq.q: How many references should I attach?
faq.a: Two or three photos of the same product from different angles. The references anchor the product's look — more angles mean fewer surprises between shots.

faq.q: Will my product stay consistent across shots?
faq.a: Yes. Every shot is generated from your references, so shape, color and details carry through the whole video.

faq.q: What if a scene needs another take?
faq.a: Generate a variation from the same brief — both versions land in the Library and you keep the stronger one. Held credits return automatically if a job fails.

steps.title: Pick a tool preset
steps.body: White background for marketplaces, lifestyle for ads, social crops for stories.

steps.title: Set ratio and references
steps.body: 1:1 for listings, 9:16 for stories; add one product photo to anchor the look.

steps.title: Watch the price confirm
steps.body: Each run quotes its credits up front — nothing is charged without a confirm.

steps.title: Collect the results
steps.body: Keep the winners, rerun the rest. Everything lands in the Library.

tip.title: Good to know
tip.body: Every run quotes its credits before it runs, and generated images stay in the Library until you delete them. Download the keepers.

faq.q: Can I get marketplace-ready white background images?
faq.a: Yes — the white-background preset produces clean main images sized for listings. Pair it with the field guide on Amazon main image rules.

faq.q: Do I need professional photos to start?
faq.a: No. A few clear phone photos are enough as references. Better input photos make better output, but nobody needs a studio.

faq.q: Can I make social crops of the same image?
faq.a: Yes — rerun the same brief with a different ratio: 1:1 for listings, 9:16 for stories, 4:5 for feeds.

tip.title: Good to know
tip.body: One card per product is enough to start. Re-import the same URL any time to refresh the photos and description.

faq.q: Which product pages can I import from?
faq.a: Any public product URL — marketplace listings, your own shop, landing pages. AI reads the photos and description that are already on the page.

faq.q: Can I fix things after the import?
faq.a: Yes. Every card is editable: rename the product, swap photos, rewrite the description. What you save is what future briefs use.

faq.q: What happens when my page changes?
faq.a: Import the URL again to refresh the card. Nothing in your library changes until you re-import.

steps.title: Pick a finished video
steps.body: Any completed job from your Library — the original stays untouched.

steps.title: Choose an operation
steps.body: Add subtitles, restyle existing ones, or translate to another language.

steps.title: Style it with live preview
steps.body: Font, size, position and color update as you click.

steps.title: Generate a new version
steps.body: A new Library entry; compare both and keep the one that reads best.

tip.title: Good to know
tip.body: Most social feeds autoplay muted, so subtitled cuts usually hold attention longer than the same video without them.

faq.q: Will the original video change?
faq.a: No. The subtitled cut is saved as a new Library entry — the original stays untouched so you can always go back.

faq.q: Can I translate the subtitles?
faq.a: Yes. Pick the translation operation and target language; the new version keeps your video and swaps the captions.

faq.q: Which style reads best on mobile?
faq.a: Bold, medium-large text in the bottom third with a subtle shadow. The live preview shows exactly what viewers will see before you burn it in.
